stableMappingPatterns.name: Trade identifier -> assignedIdentifier.value
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: FpML tradeId values are repeatedly copied into CDM assignedIdentifier.identifier.value preserving the trade identifier value (often with an associated scheme).
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Trade-level ids are high-value stable keys in the source and are preserved to allow traceability to the original FpML trade.
caveats: In some CDM outputs there are more assignedIdentifier entries than FpML tradeId elements (possible duplication or added identifiers).
AssignedIdentifier.scheme in CDM sometimes differs from FpML tradeIdScheme; reason not consistently evident from examples.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Trade date normalization (remove trailing 'Z')
stableMappingPatterns.targetPattern: trade.tradeDate.value (CDM normalized ISO date without trailing 'Z')
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Dates copied from FpML have their trailing 'Z' (UTC designator) trimmed in CDM date.value fields to produce a plain date string.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM date fields in these examples use a normalized date format without the timezone marker; mapping routine trims the 'Z' to conform to CDM expected value.
caveats: Normalization appears consistent in examples but rules for timezone-preserving conversions (if needed) are not shown.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Option product type -> CDM taxonomy name
stableMappingPatterns.targetPattern: trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value (CDM normalized taxonomy name)
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: FpML product type labels (e.g., 'Euro Binary') are normalized and mapped into a CDM taxonomy name value (e.g., 'EuroBinary').
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM uses standardized taxonomy strings for product classification; mapping normalizes source labels to the expected CDM taxonomy representations.
caveats: Normalization details (exact string transformations) are inferred from examples but not exhaustively specified across all possible productType variants.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
stableMappingPatterns.sourcePattern: expiryDateTime.expiryDate and expiryTime (FpML) and businessCenter fields
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Expiry-related fields in FpML (date, time, business center) are reshaped into CDM exerciseTerms.expiration components and time fields.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Exercise/expiration in CDM is modeled with nested date/time/business-center pieces; mapping splits and assigns the corresponding FpML pieces into those CDM fields.
caveats: Business center/timezone handling is consistent in examples but may require further rules for edge cases (e.g., missing time or multiple business centers).

stableMappingPatterns.name: Payment amounts -> CDM quantities (value + currency unit)
stableMappingPatterns.targetPattern: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and trade.tradeLot.quantity.unit.currency.value (CDM quantities with currency units)
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Each FpML paymentAmount (amount + currency) is converted to a CDM quantity with numeric value and currency unit.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM models cash/economic amounts as quantities with explicit units; mapping populates value and currency subfields from FpML paymentAmount.
caveats: When FpML uses splitSettlement or multiple paymentAmount entries some CDM examples aggregate or merge them into a single quantity.

folderLevelPrinciples: Preserve primary trade identifiers: FpML tradeId values are retained in CDM assignedIdentifier entries for traceability.
Represent monetary amounts as CDM quantities: each FpML paymentAmount (amount + currency) becomes a CDM quantity with value and currency unit.
Assemble price from rate + quoted currency pair: exchangeRate rate plus quotedCurrencyPair determine CDM price.value and the two currencies (unit/perUnitOf).
Normalize dates/times: FpML date/time strings are normalized (examples trim trailing 'Z') when placed into CDM date/value/time fields.
Map option expiry components into CDM exerciseTerms: expiry date, optional time and business center map to exerciseTerms.expiration elements.
Mapping may include enrichments: CDM often contains added metadata (taxonomy schemes) and generated party identifiers when absent in FpML.

variantsAndExceptions.name: AssignedIdentifier.scheme differences
variantsAndExceptions.description: AssignedIdentifier.scheme used in CDM sometimes differs from the tradeIdScheme present (or absent) in FpML examples.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Do not assume the scheme string is copied verbatim; mapping may normalize, override, or supplement scheme values.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Buyer/Seller role inversion
variantsAndExceptions.description: Several CDM examples show buyer/seller or payer/receiver roles appearing inverted compared to the FpML buyerPartyReference/sellerPartyReference hrefs.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Role mapping cannot be safely generalized without clarifying the rule used to derive CDM Party1/Party2 from FpML hrefs; treat buyer/seller polarity as tentative in mappings.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Duplicated tradeIdentifier entries

variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Avoid assuming a 1:1 correspondence between FpML tradeId elements and CDM tradeIdentifier list; additional identifiers may be added or duplicated during mapping.
